title: KV / prefix cache correctness evals and regression detection
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Recent model/config rollouts have occasionally produced subtle output changes when prefix/KV cache hits occur. These changes range from tokenization shifts to altered factual statements in multi-turn prompts. Because cache hits alter internal KV reuse, identical visible prompts can produce differing continuations depending on cache state; this creates regressions that are not captured by our current unit tests or high-level perf benchmarks.

Goal:
1) Create an automated eval suite that verifies cache correctness across model versions and runtime config changes (quantization, kernel scheduling, KV eviction policies).
2) Surface statistically significant divergences tied to cache hit vs cold-run behavior and tie them into the Console + alerting.
3) Provide safe rollout controls (block, warn, auto-fallback) when regression thresholds are exceeded.

Scope & non-goals:
- In-scope: KV/prefix cache correctness for text-generation and chat flows for open models in our catalog, runtime config toggles that affect cache behavior, integration with nightly CI and Console alerts.
- Out-of-scope for this ticket: full model-level quality evals unrelated to cache effects (handled by evals-team), large-scale human labeling effort (we will trigger sample human reviews when automated signals exceed thresholds).

Why this matters now:
- Dedicated customers reported intermittent semantic changes after a recent kernel scheduling tweak (ENG-4681).
- Our rollout automation currently depends on token-level regression metrics alone; cache-specific divergence patterns require more targeted instrumentation and analysis.

High-level approach:
1) Build an eval harness that compares paired runs: (a) cold-start (no KV/prefix) and (b) warm-start (with synthetic prefix or KV priming) across a deterministic suite of prompts and seedable RNG.
2) Create a deterministic baseline store keyed by (model, quantization_profile, runtime-config-hash, prompt-set-version). Baselines are stored as newline-delimited outputs + embeddings for semantic comparison.
3) Compute a set of metrics per run: exact token diffs, normalized Levenshtein, semantic cosine similarity (embedding based), and output-level classifier flags (hallucination/factuality heuristics).
4) Statistical test: run N=50 pairs per prompt set (more for high-variance prompts). Use paired bootstrap or Wilcoxon signed-rank to detect systematic shifts.
5) Integrate with Console: create an alert when divergence_rate > threshold OR mean semantic similarity < threshold for any model+config. Provide diff snapshots, top-k divergent prompts, and example traces.

Acceptance criteria:
- Eval harness can run nightly for all production models and runtime configs we ship (proof: sample run in CI).
- Alerts surface in Console with links to raw diffs and run metadata.
- A documented rollback/playbook exists for when a cache-related regression is detected (manual rollback + auto-fallback to cache-bypass variant).
- Regression detection false-positive rate under controlled experiments < 10% (measured on historical data).

Design notes & trade-offs:
- Deterministic vs stochastic: We will seed RNG where possible, but true model nondeterminism (sampling temperature) requires multiple samples. We will default to nucleus-sampling with fixed seeds for comparisons and include a uniform-temperature run for stress testing.
- Cost vs coverage: Full exhaustive runs across every prompt and model variant are expensive. We'll tier prompt sets: smoke (50 prompts), canonical (500 prompts across user flows), legal/compliance (100 prompts). Nightly runs will execute smoke+canonical for high-risk models; full suites run weekly.
- Semantic similarity: Relying solely on token diffs is brittle (minor tokenization differences). We'll compute embedding cosine similarity (average of top-3 completions) and a compact classifier for semantic drift trained on historical cache regressions.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for harness components (output normalize, diff computation, metrics).
- Synthetic fuzzer that introduces controlled cache corruption to verify detection sensitivity. (See test vector generator in linked repo).
- Canary run for runtime-1.22 in dedicated staging cluster with telemetry gate before any rollout to production.

Rollout & mitigation:
- Step 1: Deploy harness + nightly runner to staging. Monitor divergence metrics for two weeks.
- Step 2: For any model/config exceeding thresholds, block rollout to production and trigger auto-fallback to cache-bypass variant for existing traffic.
- Step 3: Post-incident: capture full traces, pin to working kernel set, create remediation ticket.
